item.text: The page currently waits for the dashboard API before returning any markup, so the route’s loading fallback is the only thing users can see while it waits. I’m moving that request behind section-level Suspense boundaries and sharing one request across them, so the page heading and useful placeholders can be part of the prerendered shell.

The shell now starts the API request once and lets the stats, revenue, and invoices sections await the same promise independently. That preserves the single backend call while giving each section its own prerendered fallback.

item.text:
Updated [app/page.tsx](/workspace/app/page.tsx:47) so the dashboard heading and section fallbacks can render in the partial pre-rendered shell while the API request is pending. Stats, revenue, and invoices now await the same data promise behind separate Suspense boundaries, keeping the single API request and allowing the sections to resolve independently.

I didn’t run tests. `package.json` and `package-lock.json` were already changed in the workspace; I left them untouched.
